## Choosing the Right Test

| Data Type | Groups | Test |
|-----------|--------|------|
| Continuous | 1 sample vs value | One-sample t-test |
| Continuous | 2 independent groups | Two-sample t-test |
| Continuous | 2 paired groups | Paired t-test |
| Continuous | 3+ groups | One-way ANOVA |
| Continuous | 2 variables | Correlation/Regression |
| Categorical | 2 categories | Chi-square test |

## Descriptive Statistics

```r
# Basic stats
mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)
median(x, na.rm = TRUE)
sd(x, na.rm = TRUE)
var(x, na.rm = TRUE)
min(x); max(x); range(x)
quantile(x, probs = c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75))

# Summary
summary(data)

# By group
data |>
  group_by(group) |>
  summarize(
    n = n(),
    mean = mean(outcome),
    sd = sd(outcome),
    se = sd / sqrt(n)
  )
```

## t-tests

### One-Sample t-test
*Is the mean different from a specific value?*

```r
t.test(x, mu = 100)
```

### Two-Sample t-test (Independent)
*Do two groups have different means?*

```r
# Two vectors
t.test(group1, group2)

# Formula syntax
t.test(outcome ~ group, data = data)

# Assume equal variance
t.test(outcome ~ group, data = data, var.equal = TRUE)
```

### Paired t-test
*Before/after measurements on same subjects*

```r
t.test(before, after, paired = TRUE)
```

## ANOVA

### One-Way ANOVA
*Compare means across 3+ groups*

```r
model <- aov(outcome ~ group, data = data)
summary(model)
```

### Post-hoc Test (Tukey's HSD)
*Which groups differ?*

```r
TukeyHSD(model)
```

### Two-Way ANOVA
*Two factors*

```r
model <- aov(outcome ~ factor1 * factor2, data = data)
summary(model)
```

## Correlation

### Pearson Correlation
*Linear relationship between continuous variables*

```r
cor(x, y)
cor.test(x, y)
```

### Spearman Correlation
*Ranked/ordinal data*

```r
cor.test(x, y, method = "spearman")
```

### Correlation Matrix
```r
cor(data[, c("var1", "var2", "var3")])
```

## Linear Regression

### Simple Regression
*One predictor*

```r
model <- lm(y ~ x, data = data)
summary(model)
```

### Multiple Regression
*Multiple predictors*

```r
model <- lm(y ~ x1 + x2 + x3, data = data)
summary(model)
```

### Tidy Output with broom
```r
library(broom)
tidy(model)    # Coefficients
glance(model)  # Model stats
augment(model) # Fitted values
```

## Checking Assumptions

### Normality
```r
shapiro.test(x)                    # Shapiro-Wilk test
qqnorm(x); qqline(x)               # Q-Q plot
hist(x)                            # Histogram
```

### Homogeneity of Variance
```r
bartlett.test(outcome ~ group, data = data)
car::leveneTest(outcome ~ group, data = data)
```

### Residual Diagnostics
```r
plot(model)  # Four diagnostic plots
```

## Non-parametric Alternatives

| Parametric | Non-parametric |
|------------|----------------|
| One-sample t | `wilcox.test(x, mu = ...)` |
| Two-sample t | `wilcox.test(x, y)` |
| Paired t | `wilcox.test(x, y, paired = TRUE)` |
| ANOVA | `kruskal.test(outcome ~ group, data)` |
| Correlation | `cor.test(x, y, method = "spearman")` |

## Chi-Square Test

### Test of Independence
```r
table <- table(data$var1, data$var2)
chisq.test(table)
```

### Goodness of Fit
```r
chisq.test(observed, p = expected_proportions)
```

## Interpreting P-values

| P-value | Interpretation |
|---------|----------------|
| p < 0.001 | Highly significant (***) |
| p < 0.01 | Very significant (**) |
| p < 0.05 | Significant (*) |
| p >= 0.05 | Not significant |

## Interpreting Correlation (r)

| |r| | Strength |
|-----|----------|
| 0.0 - 0.3 | Weak |
| 0.3 - 0.5 | Moderate |
| 0.5 - 0.7 | Strong |
| 0.7 - 1.0 | Very strong |

## Interpreting R-squared

R² = proportion of variance explained by the model

- R² = 0.50 means 50% of variance is explained
- Higher is better (0 to 1)
- Adjusted R² accounts for number of predictors

## Quick Decision Tree

```
Is your outcome continuous?
├── Yes
│   ├── Comparing to a value? → One-sample t-test
│   ├── Comparing 2 groups?
│   │   ├── Same subjects? → Paired t-test
│   │   └── Different subjects? → Two-sample t-test
│   ├── Comparing 3+ groups? → ANOVA
│   └── Relationship with another variable? → Correlation/Regression
└── No (categorical)
    └── Comparing proportions? → Chi-square test
```
